statement: Make finalize() in codes/loop/loop.sbatch classify a scheduler termination as neither a clean cycle nor a failure. Reproduced offline (evidence/loop_resume/validation_repair_harness.txt scenario K): with the loop running, SIGTERM to the link's process group - what slurmstepd sends at the 2-23:30:00 time limit and on scancel, followed by SIGKILL after KillWait 30 s - makes bash 5.1.8 run the EXIT trap, and finalize logs 'clean exit -- failcount reset to 0' (3 of 3 runs; also when only bash is signalled) or, when the child is signalled first, 'failure rc=143 -- failcount now 1/3' with the successor kept; three links of the latter kind trip the breaker and scancel a healthy chain, and the former resets the breaker on a link whose loop was killed mid-cycle. Second conjunct (scenario L): a loop exit code 3 is treated as a storage stop (successor cancelled, uncounted) even when STOP was not written, so any stage that happens to exit 3 under bash -e ends the chain silently. Fix shape: trap TERM (and optionally an sbatch --signal=B:USR1@N warning) to set a flag before the loop starts; in finalize, when the flag is set or the loop's status is 128+15, log 'scheduler termination', leave .failcount unchanged and keep the successor; treat RC==KTG_RC_SCRATCH_STOP as a chain stop only if $BASEDIR/STOP exists, else count it as a failure. Closes by a result row whose offline injection run adds: SIGTERM to the process group over three consecutive links -> .failcount unchanged, no scancel, successor kept; child-first and bash-only orderings -> the same; loop exit 3 without STOP -> counted as a failure. The executed proof under a real scheduler stays with o25.
